text:
taylor: Heads-up 5-minute sync: ACME trial-to-commit flow. Partner wants a marketplace private-offer that protects customers from overage sticker shock in month 1. Idea: a 30-day overage protection buffer (we eat first 10% overage) + graduated renewal discount ladder if they convert. Thoughts?

mina: I like the buffer. Practical question: do marketplaces allow negative adjustments like that on first invoice? AWS yes as a credit line; GCP unclear for auto-applied protection.

jen: If GCP can't auto-apply, we can issue a one-time promo code/voucher post-invoice that credits account. That needs reconciliation though. 

marco: From finance POV, we need deterministic limits. Suggest cap the protection at $25k or 10% whichever is smaller, to bound risk. Also need to map to revenue recognition: credits against ARR or contra-revenue? Legal/finance call.

taylor: Good point. Let's cap it. Proposal: protection = min(10% of month1 bill, $25k). Renewal ladder if they commit within 60 days: 8% first-year renewal credit, 4% second year, then standard pricing.

mina: Sales/field note: make the ladder visible in listing but call it "commit conversion incentives" rather than "credits". Simpler message for customers.

jen: Ops question: how do we tag these in Console/Optimize? If it's a negative line item we should set metadata: credit_reason:overage_protection, offer:acme-trial. Then analytics can exclude it from unit economics.

marco: Agree. We also need a fraud/gaming clause. Example: if customer intentionally spikes usage to trigger protection then drops, we void. Legal draft needed.

ops-bot: Reminder: marketplace listing checklist incomplete: SI playbook, billing mapping, legal clause, partner collateral.

taylor: Technical approach: don't change serving SKU. Apply credit as billing adjustment event. Schema proposal:
```
{"event_type":"credit_adjustment","cust":"C789","offer":"ACME-TRIAL-2026","reason":"overage_protection","amount_usd":12000,"cap_usd":25000}
```
This keeps runtime untouched and gives ops an audit trail.

mina: That works. Please include partner_id and marketplace_id fields too so partner ops can reconcile.

jen: Also add a flag `applied_automatically: true|false` because for GCP we might need manual voucher issuance.

marco: For renewal ladder accounting: treat renewal credits as deferred rebates that amortize over the renewal period. Finance to confirm.

mina: One more sales ask: can we surface an estimated time-to-value micro-metric in the listing? e.g., "Avg setup: 2-4 weeks; expected inference cost savings: 30% after tuning". Helps drive conversion.

taylor: Yes include in copy. But we must set guardrails so numbers are not promises. Use phrasing: "typical" or "median".

jen: Action items: (1) Marco: confirm cap & rev rec approach with finance (2) Mina: draft marketplace copy and SI quickstart (3) Jen: billing event schema PR + ops runbook (4) Taylor: draft legal clause for anti-gaming and credit T&Cs.

marco: I'll ping finance; target EOD for cap confirmation.

mina: I'll share copy by tomorrow noon.

jen: I'll open PR and include `applied_automatically` flag and partner/marketplace ids.

ops-bot: Event created: ACME trial-offer finalization 500 (in 1h). Invitees: taylor, mina, jen, marco.

taylor: Cool. If we approve caps and legal language in the follow-up, we can push private-offer live next Tuesday.

mina: One-line for listing draft: "30-day overage protection + conversion incentives when you commit within 60 days."

marco: Fine with that wording.

jen: No blockers on billing side after schema PR.
